subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU, TPS, concurrency, token mix
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finapps.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU, TPS, concurrency, token mix

Hi Sam — great to meet on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size Dedicated capacity for FinApps: 

Summary from call:
- Deployment mode: FinApps is leaning toward Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for predictable latency and data isolation. Private VPC was discussed but would be a follow-up if required.
- Primary model family: customer engineering will run a quantized open model (13B–33B class) for conversational assistants; exact model TBD.
- Expected traffic: average ~40 requests/sec (RPS) during business hours, with bursts up to ~120 RPS for short periods.
- Token mix: average prompt length ~180 tokens, average completion ~420 tokens, so ~600 tokens per request on average. Peak requests may hit longer completions (~1k tokens).
- Latency SLO: 300–500ms p95 target for chat-style interactions.

Sizing questions we need from you to finalize a sizing proposal:
1) Can you confirm whether the traffic numbers above are requests-per-second (RPS) or some other TPS definition (e.g., tokens/sec)?
2) What % of traffic requires the full 1k token context vs short-turns (<300 tokens)?
3) Expected concurrency (number of simultaneous open chats/users)?
4) Any hard constraints on GPU types (preference for H100, A100, or cost-sensitive to A100/T4)?

Next steps:
- I attached a capacity_workbook.xlsx with fields for average/peak RPS, token distribution, and concurrency — please fill and return.
- I’ll loop in Aditya (infrastructure) and Rafael (solutions) to propose GPU mapping and a concrete Dedicated config.
- If helpful, we can book a deep sizing call next week to walk through numbers.

Thanks — if you want to confirm times I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The numbers I gave are RPS (requests per second). We instrument at the request level rather than tokens/sec.
- Typical distribution: ~70% of requests are short (<= 300 tokens total), ~25% are mid (300–800 tokens), ~5% are long (~800–1200 tokens).
- Average concurrent sessions during peak: ~600 concurrent users (we see many short-lived websocket sessions). Peak concurrency can spike to ~1,200 during product launches.
- Preferred GPU: we’d like H100s if available (we prioritize latency). If the price delta is large, we can consider A100s.

I’ll get the capacity_workbook back to you by EOD Friday. Priya (cc’d) will follow up from procurement on contract/start dates.

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU, TPS, concurrency, token mix

Looping in a concise recommendation based on the traffic profile Sam shared. I’ll keep it high-level; we can refine during a sizing call. 

Assumptions:
- Model class: quantized 13B–33B, sequence length up to 1k tokens for long requests.
- Average tokens/request: ~600 tokens.
- p95 latency target: 300–500ms.
- We’ll use continuous batching + KV cache to improve throughput for repeated contexts.

Recommendation (initial Dedicated config):
- Preferred GPU: H100 (best latency + perf for large-context quantized models).
- Suggested cluster: 4 x H100 (each with NVLink) for the primary Dedicated pool.
  - Expected sustained capacity: ~40–60 RPS for heavy 1k-token requests per GPU cluster in distributed setup, aggregate ~160–240 RPS sustained depending on batching and kernel optimizations.
  - Headroom for bursts: can absorb short spikes up to ~350 RPS with autoscaling/burst policies (if you budget burst capacity).
- Alternative: A100s — need ~6 x A100 to match the same sustained RPS for the 1k-token workload (higher cost in aggregate latency-sensitive money due to less headroom).
- Concurrency & batching: plan for at least 200 concurrent in-flight requests to keep GPUs well-utilized; Redwood runtime will do adaptive batching (we’ll tune batch cap, max tokens per batch).
- Memory/quantization note: use int8/quantized kernels for 13B; for 33B we’ll need model sharding or tensor parallelism — plan GPU count upwards if moving to 33B.

Next steps from infra side:
1) If FinApps confirms H100 preference, we’ll size for 4x H100 as baseline and include a burst policy to handle launches.
2) We’ll run a quick pilot on a subset of traffic (can be routed via Redwood Dedicated test pool) to validate latency and token economics.
3) Rafael will produce a formal proposal with cost/throughput mapping and suggested SLOs.

I’ll be available for a deep sizing call Wednesday 10–12 PT or Thursday 1–4 PT — pick a time and I’ll set the invite.

Aditya
